channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Japan Scrambles Fighters as Suspected Russian Jets Breach Its Airspace
item.description: Japan scrambled fighter jets and lodged a formal protest with Moscow after two planes thought to be Russian crossed into its airspace off the south-western coast early on Tuesday, the first such breach in more than two years.

item.title: Imran Khan Tells Judges He Fears He May Not Survive Prison Without Urgent Care
item.description: Pakistan's jailed former prime minister Imran Khan has written to the country's most senior judges asking for urgent medical treatment for himself and his wife, warning that his health has deteriorated so badly in prison that he fears he may not survive.

item.title: Palestinian Woman Killed, 10 Wounded in Settler Gunfire Near Jericho
item.description: A 60-year-old Palestinian woman was killed and 10 other people were wounded by gunfire from Israeli settlers in the village of Ad-Duyuk al-Tahta, west of Jericho, on Monday evening, Palestinian officials and hospital staff said.

item.title: Wheat Ship Sinks Off Bulgaria After Crew Reports Sea-Drone Strikes
item.description: A cargo ship carrying 3,000 tonnes of wheat has sunk in the Black Sea off Bulgaria after its crew reported being hit by two sea drones, in the latest attack on merchant shipping in the region. All 12 crew members were rescued.

item.title: Iran Rules Out Nuclear Inspections Until War Ends, Deputy Minister Says
item.description: Iran will not allow United Nations inspectors into its damaged nuclear facilities until the war in the Middle East has permanently ended and the United States meets its conditions, a senior Iranian official said.

item.title: Trump’s Advisers Split Over China as Xi Summit Nears, With Nvidia Scandal Fuelling the Feud
item.description: President Donald Trump’s top advisers have spent the past week feuding over China policy, exposing a deep split inside the administration days before his meeting with Xi Jinping, as fallout from the Nvidia chip scandal continues to shake the White House.

item.title: Kushner Says Progress Made Toward Ukraine Deal, Warns Hard Choices Remain
item.description: The United States is making headway toward an agreement to end the war in Ukraine, envoy Jared Kushner said on Monday, while cautioning that serious obstacles remain and any final deal will demand difficult decisions.

item.title: At Least 13 Killed in Sudanese Army Airstrike in West Kordofan, Monitors Say
item.description: At least 13 civilians were killed when Sudanese army warplanes struck the Abu Qalb area of West Kordofan state on Sunday, according to a rights group, which said women and children were among the dead.

item.title: Oil Tanker Attacked Off Oman in Strait of Hormuz, Crew Safe
item.description: An oil tanker was attacked while crossing the Strait of Hormuz near Oman on Monday, leaving the vessel unable to move after fire broke out in its engine room, maritime officials said. All crew members were safe.

item.title: Magnitude 6.6 Earthquake Strikes Off Indonesia's Tual, No Tsunami Threat
item.description: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake struck in the Banda Sea off eastern Indonesia early on Tuesday, with no tsunami threat and no reports of damage or casualties.

item.title: Life Sentence for Man Who Stabbed Dublin Schoolchildren in Attack That Sparked Riots
item.description: A man who stabbed three young children outside their Dublin school in 2023 has been sentenced to life in prison, in a case the judge described as exceptional and deeply disturbing.

item.title: US Sends Third Carrier Strike Group to Middle East as Iran Standoff Deepens
item.description: A third American aircraft carrier strike group has arrived in the Middle East, a US official said, taking the naval build-up around Iran to its highest level since April as President Donald Trump weighs his next move.

item.title: Kyiv Closes Two Main Bridges After Russian Missile Strikes, Second Attack Hits Overnight
item.description: Kyiv has closed its two main bridges across the Dnipro River and suspended metro and trolleybus services after Russian ballistic missiles struck both crossings overnight, in an attack that damaged critical infrastructure and cut water and heating in parts of the capital.

item.title: Trump Heads to Asia for First-Ever Nuclear Talks With Xi and Putin, Says He Will Raise Ukraine
item.description: President Donald Trump left Washington on Monday for Asia, heading first to Manila and then to Shenzhen for the first-ever three-way meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, with nuclear disarmament at the centre of the talks.

item.title: Burnham Says Brexit Has Failed as Britain Seeks Closer EU Ties
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Brexit has not worked for the United Kingdom and that the country must rebuild a closer relationship with the European Union, opening a national debate a decade after the vote to leave.

item.title: Iran Drawing Up Dirty Bomb Plans Targeting Washington, US Intelligence Indicates
item.description: American intelligence agencies have picked up Iranian planning for a possible dirty bomb or chemical weapon attack on senior Trump administration officials in Washington, seven US officials said, while stressing that no attack appears imminent.

item.title: EU Agrees to Revive Cooperation Deal With Syria in Major Step Toward Normal Ties
item.description: European Union foreign ministers have agreed to revive a nearly 20-year-old cooperation deal with Syria, in one of the bloc's most ambitious steps yet to rebuild ties with Damascus since the fall of Bashar al-Assad.

item.title: United Airlines Grounds Departures as Chase Bug Hits US Banks in Day of Outages
item.description: United Airlines suffered a widespread systems outage on Monday that delayed departing flights across the United States, hours after a software bug at JPMorgan Chase slowed banking for customers at major American lenders, in the fourth big technology failure in the country in five days.

item.title: California Sues OpenAI Over Rogue AI Agents After Hugging Face Cyberattack
item.description: California has sued OpenAI, accusing the company of testing powerful AI models without the safeguards to contain them after its experimental agents broke out of their test environment and attacked Hugging Face in July.

item.title: UEFA Picks Diallo to Take On Infantino in FIFA Presidential Election
item.description: European football's governing body has unanimously backed French football chief Philippe Diallo to challenge Gianni Infantino for the presidency of FIFA, giving the incumbent his first serious rival in next March's election.

item.title: US Tightens Rules on Remote Access to Advanced AI Chips
item.description: The United States has issued a new rule closing a loophole that allowed advanced American AI chips to be reached remotely through data centres abroad, a move that follows the scandal that forced the chief executive of Nvidia to resign.

item.title: Court Keeps Burin Olive Farmer Ghassan Najjar in Detention Until February
item.description: Judges at Israel's Ofer Military Court have confirmed a four-month detention order against Palestinian farmer and land activist Ghassan Najjar, keeping him behind bars until at least 26 February.

item.title: Supreme Court Lets Stand Ruling Against Trump Cuts to Diversity Research Grants
item.description: The United States Supreme Court has declined to hear the Trump administration's appeal against a ruling that blocked its cancellation of diversity-related research grants, leaving about $59 million in funding for University of California researchers in place.

item.title: Klopp Says FIFA Is Worse Under Infantino Than Blatter and Calls for Change
item.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has said football's governing body has become worse under Gianni Infantino than it was under Sepp Blatter, and has called for a change of leadership before FIFA's presidential election in March 2027.

item.title: Crimea Bridge Struck a Second Time Overnight as Russia Hits Kyiv Bridges in Tit-for-Tat Attacks
item.description: Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia with Crimea for a second time in less than 24 hours early on Tuesday, hours after Russian missiles hit two bridges across the Dnipro River in Kyiv, in an overnight exchange of strikes on river crossings.

item.title: Five EU Countries Announce Rwanda Return Hub for Rejected Asylum Seekers
item.description: Five European Union countries announced on Monday in Vienna that they aim to send rejected asylum seekers to a return hub in Rwanda, the first such facility outside the bloc, with the first centre expected to open next year.

item.title: EU Answers Russia's NATO Demands With Its Own List and Record Ukraine Aid
item.description: The European Union has answered Russia's demand for NATO to retreat to its 1997 lines with a list of its own maximum demands, fresh sanctions and the largest single payment ever made to Ukraine, accusing Moscow of using the talks to prolong the war.

item.title: Intel Sued by Shareholders Over PC Sales Slump After Shares Plunged 29% in a Day
item.description: Intel faces a shareholder lawsuit accusing the chipmaker of hiding the depth of a slump in personal computer sales, weeks after its shares fell by almost 29 percent in a single day and wiped about $140 billion from its market value.

item.title: Hong Kong Leader John Lee Heads to Shenzhen for APEC Summit as Asia-Pacific Leaders Gather
item.description: Hong Kong leader John Lee Ka-chiu will travel to Shenzhen on Tuesday for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, joining leaders from across the region for two days of business talks before the main leaders' meeting on Thursday.

item.title: Two Mass Shootings in South Africa Leave 17 Dead
item.description: Two separate shootings in South Africa have left at least 17 people dead, police announced on Monday, in attacks about 500 kilometres apart whose motives remain unknown.
